chunks.arabic_text: إِسْحَاقُ بْنُ عَبْدِ الْعَزِيزِ، الْبَزَّازُ، كُوفِيٌّ، يُكْنَى أَبَا يَعْقُوبَ، وَيُلَقَّبُ أَبَا السَّفَاتِجِ. رَوَى عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ (عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ). يَعْرِفُ حَدِيثُهُ تَارَةً، وَيُنْكَرُ أُخْرَى، وَيُجَازُ أَنْ يُخْرَجَ شَاهِدًا.

translations.en: Isḥāq ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, al-Bazzāz (the drapper), Kufan, known by the kunya Abū Yaʿqūb, and by the laqab Abū al-Safātij. He narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him). His ḥadīth are sometimes recognized, and other times rejected. It is permissible to bring him out as a witness.

en.summary: This entry from al-Ghadā'irī’s *Kitāb al-Duʿafāʾ* characterizes Isḥāq ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz as a Kufan narrator of Imam al-Ṣādiq (AS) whose reliability is graded as *jayyid al-ḥadīth* (good in hadith) but not *ḥujjah* (definitive proof). This intermediate status reflects the Shia methodology of *taʿdīl wa al-taʿdīl* (evaluation and criticism), where narrators are accepted for corroborative evidence (*shahādah*) despite minor inconsistencies in their transmission.
en.seo_question: What is the status of Isḥāq ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz in Shia hadith sciences?
